newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids near midday Monday were light at $62.00 to $63.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00 to $65.00, feedlot sources said.
"It looks like an inventory day today," a Kansas feedlot manager said.
Packer buyers were checking feedlot inventories as they gauged needs for next week, the manager said.
Sales activity this week was expected by Wednesday so packers and feedlots could wrap up business before the Independence Day holiday on Friday, several sources said.

Fed cattle price outlooks this week were mixed, with those looking for steady-firm prices citing expected spillover strength from steep advances in hog prices after USDA's bullish quarterly Hogs and Pigs report.
Projections for steady-weak prices were primed by outlooks for increased market-ready cattle supplies during July and softer beef demand after the upcoming long holiday weekend.

Showlists this week were seen mostly unchanged from last week, which could lend support, but that strength could crumble if beef prices continue lower after a brief respite from last week's precipitous declines, they said.
